prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the geometry of a small bathroom under renovation with two open doorways in the back-left and centre-left walls (receding to 3–4 m in dark grey/black) and a bright, near vertical shower wall on the right (within 0.3–0.8 m of the camera wearer). Across frames 1 to 3, it clearly separates two people on the left: a woman in a green headband standing 1.2–1.5 m away in front of the left wall and a man standing about 1.0–1.5 m further behind her (~2.5–3.0 m from the camera) in the hallway doorway, while the camera wearer's left hand enters the bottom edge at ~0.3 m. In frames 4 and 5, as the camera wearer turns right and approaches the orange-boarded shower wall (bringing the wall surface to 0.3–0.5 m and an overhead shower arm into the upper-right foreground), both arms and a handheld power drill held in the right hand appear brightly within arm's reach (~0.2–0.4 m) while the other people move out of view to the left. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map makes the continuous distance gradient along the floor, the recess of the adjacent closet and hallway, and the exact proximity of the right-hand wall and drill bit immediately apparent. However, the depth map is unreliable around fine structures and boundaries, smoothing over the wall-mounted circular plate, blurring the thin drill bit into the wall plane in frame 5, and losing internal facial and limb relief on the distant man inside the dark doorway.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates human silhouettes in the scene while leaving all architectural features, doorways, and tools unlabelled in black. In frames 1 to 3, it segments the nearer woman on the left (~1.2–1.5 m away, facing right toward the camera wearer in frame 1 before turning toward the man in the doorway in frames 2 and 3) as a brown mask and the further man in the doorway behind her (~2.5–3.0 m away, facing forward toward the room) as a pink mask about 1–1.5 m behind and slightly above her on the image plane. In frame 2, a small cyan 'person' mask also captures the camera wearer's own left hand at the bottom edge (~0.3 m away), and in frame 4, as the camera pans right toward the wall, a brown mask labels the camera wearer's outstretched left arm (~0.3–0.4 m away) while a tiny pink mask at the far bottom-left edge captures the occluded lower leg and foot of the person still standing ~1.5 m to the left. This map makes it easier than RGB alone to see the exact pixel boundary and minimal overlap between the nearer woman's raised left arm and the man standing behind her in frames 2 and 3, as well as the sliver of a person remaining at the far left edge in frame 4. However, the segmentation is unreliable in several places: it merges the camera wearer's bottom-left hand into the nearer woman's leg mask in frame 1, misses the camera wearer's right hand holding the drill in frame 4 and both arms completely in frame 5, and fails to segment any objects such as the cordless drill, shower fixture, or wall panels.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D skeletal keypoints for visible bodies in yellow and hands in magenta against a black background. Across frames 1 to 3, it tracks the full-body skeleton of the man standing ~2.5–3.0 m away in the doorway, showing his torso and shoulders squared toward the camera wearer and the nearer woman, with his arms bent at the elbows in front of his waist in frames 1 and 2 before dropping his left arm to his side in frame 3. It also detects magenta hand skeletons for the camera wearer's own left hand in the bottom foreground (~0.3–0.4 m away, within arm's reach of the wall) in frame 1 and again in frame 4 as the camera turns toward the right wall. Compared to the RGB strip, the yellow skeleton clarifies the distant man's upright posture, hip-width stance, and elbow articulation inside the dimly lit doorway, while the magenta keypoints in frame 4 trace the finger curl of the camera wearer's raised left hand against the wall edge. However, the pose map is highly incomplete and unreliable overall: it completely misses the nearer woman (~1.2–1.5 m away) across all frames despite her being unoccluded in frames 1–3, fails to detect the man's partially visible leg at the left edge of frame 4, and misses the camera wearer's right hand gripping the drill in frames 4 and 5 as well as the left hand in frames 2, 3, and 5.
